top.line: When agents can build anything, direction is scarce
top.para: The rule, used since my CISO days, is to work at the place of highest leverage: most value now, unblocked, startable without knowing the end. Three days of newsroom work show it, from a reading meter to a vault pane, with two steps walked back and a branch parked. Shoulders that are commodities made it fast.

short.line: Work where the next step moves the needle most
short.para: Agents cannot supply the sense of what to build and when to stop. Start without knowing how it ends, ship each step to a user, even yourself, and accept that the path is five choices at every step. Walking back and parking are not failures, mature shoulders speed things up, and briefs depend on what shipped.

rule.line: Work only on unblocked steps that change the most
rule.para: The rule says where to stand, not what to build, and the first step's job is to inform the second. It resembles Fermi estimates, Bayesian updating and Monte Carlo ranges, where a first bad guess narrows into a useful range. Constraints make it work, as Dan Ward's FIRE model says, and saying no is most of the work.

steps.line: Each step was chosen after using the last
steps.para: On 10 October the meter, pay by depth, personas, encrypted sharing and usefulness pricing shipped within hours. On 11 October came persona and reading-list links, and the passkey door was removed, then restored at 00:15 when a lab found phone QR passkeys return different bytes. Wire automation and analytics are parked until there are many readers.

back.line: Walking back and parking are moves, not failures
back.para: Removing and restoring the door were two-way doors, in Bezos's sense, each costing an afternoon, the second forced by a test. A parked branch stays on the map with a dated reason. Backwards the path looks inevitable; forwards there were choices like a paywall, accounts or Google sign-in, and shipping each step replaces foresight.

map.line: Standing on mature shoulders made the passkey work fast
map.para: The passkey work went from genesis to product in a day because it sits on commodities: synced iCloud passkeys with PRF, Web Crypto, the vendored vault library, Stripe. The custom layer is small. The exception, Google Password Manager over QR returning different bytes, is where a door per path was needed and work slowed.

ship.line: Every step must be shipped and used straight away
ship.para: Each piece of work must be opened by a person, even if that person is me, not left as a design document. A shipped step shows where the next is; a designed one teaches nothing. The site is an inbox could not have been written two days earlier, because the art of the possible comes from shipping.

limits.line: Three days is a sample, and parking has costs
limits.para: The sequence and times come from release logs but cover one project at one speed. The rule chooses where to stand, not what to build, and the mathematical analogy is not a theorem. A parked branch may be overtaken and need rebuilding, a cost accepted as cheaper than building for absent readers.

sources.line: Sources: release logs, the newsroom articles and quotations
sources.para: A voice memo of 12 October 2026 and the release logs of sgit.ai and newsroom.sgit.ai from 10 to 12 October, with articles such as Pay after you read and The vault is live. Also Bezos's 2015 shareholder letter, a Steve Jobs line quoted from memory and Dan Ward's FIRE model.
